chunks: Al-Nadr narrated from Durust, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Muyassir, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

When this verse was revealed: 'And do not extend your eyes to that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, the finery of worldly life,' the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sat up straight and then said: 'Whoever does not take solace with the consolation of Allah will have his soul cut off with regrets for the world; and whoever follows with his gaze what is in the hands of people, his anxiety will be prolonged and his thirst will not be quenched; and whoever does not recognize Allah's blessings upon him except in food or drink, his action will fall short and his chastisement will be near.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the verse 'Do not extend your eyes' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Prophet’s (SAWW) physical reaction to Quran 20:131, emphasizing that true contentment (*qana'ah*) requires anchoring the heart in divine consolation rather than worldly comparison. It warns that reducing God’s blessings (*ni'am*) solely to material sustenance (*mat'am* and *mashrab*) leads to spiritual diminishment and accelerated punishment, a key concept in Shia asceticism (*zuhd*).

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Al-Naḍr narrated from Durust, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Muyassir, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

When the following verse was revealed: Do not gaze longingly at what We have given some of them to enjoy, the [fleeting] finery of this worldly life… (Q20:131), the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) sat up straight and then said, ‘Whoever does not take solace with the consolation of Allah will overwhelm himself with [sorrow and] regret for [what he has lost of] this world; and whoever follows with his gaze that which is in the possession of others, his sadness will be prolonged and his anger will never subside; and whoever does not recognize the blessing of Allah upon him except in his food or drink, his action will fall short and his chastisement will be near.’”
